summary: Office IoT multicast storm on corporate floor causes Zero Trust overlay disconnects and internal DNS stalls
description:
Issue summary:

On 2026-03-10 morning, staff on the SF office corporate SSID experienced intermittent inability to reach internal services (Confluence, internal API endpoints) while Internet connectivity remained nominal. Sessions to internal services would hang or reset; internal DNS queries for internal hostnames would take several seconds or fail. Impact was concentrated on the 4th floor office area.

Impact:
- ~20% of active users on the 4th floor reported degraded access between 08:50 and 10:20 PST.
- Internal service health checks did not show upstream failures; client-side overlays (Zero Trust agent) reported frequent connection resets.

Environment:
- Wireless controller: Aruba 8400 cluster, controller firmware 8.6.0-12 (affected APs running 6.3.1.7).
- APs: Aruba AP-515 (802.11ax) on 5GHz DFS channels in sector A3.
- Zero-trust agent: redwood-zt-client v1.4.3 on macOS and Windows clients.
- Internal DNS: core-dns cluster behind edge-firewall (internal-only).
- Switching: leaf switches on 4th floor with default IGMP snooping disabled.

Initial hypothesis:
- Excessive multicast/broadcast traffic from IoT devices on a bridged VLAN caused AP CPU saturation and the wireless controller to drop or queue traffic. That in turn caused socket stalls for the Zero Trust overlay and promoted DNS query queuing at the edge, leading to the observed failures.

Observed facts:
- AP CPU peaked >95% during the incident window.
- Conntrack table on the affected APs reported >95% utilization.
- Zero-trust agent logs show repeated TLS socket reset and rekey attempts coincident with the AP CPU spikes.
- DNS server metrics show short-term query latency spikes (p99 ~1.2s) during the same period.

Suggested next steps: rate-limit mDNS/LLMNR on the office SSID, enable IGMP snooping on floor switches, and move IoT devices to an isolated SSID/VLAN.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Place an inexpensive consumer IoT camera on the same VLAN as corporate-ssid in sector A3.
2) Enable heavy mDNS probe behavior (simulated with mdns-replay tool sending ~4000 queries/min).
3) Observe AP CPU and conntrack counters; monitor Zero Trust agent logs and DNS query latency from a client on the same SSID.
4) Confirm that repeated mDNS bursts correlate with Zero Trust socket resets and DNS query queuing on core-dns.
logs: 2026-03-10T08:52:13Z zt-client[pid=2234] WARN tls: connection reset by peer, attempting reconnect
Syslog snippet from leaf-switch-4F: IGMP snooping disabled; multicast flood threshold exceeded
investigation_notes: Network team captured PCAP at AP uplink: sustained mDNS/LLMNR packets to 224.0.0.251:5353 and 239.255.255.250:1900 from a set of consumer mac addresses.
AP CPU profile shows multicast processing hot path consuming >60% of cycles in kernel packet handling (firmware-level issue suspected).
Conntrack state indicates large number of ephemeral UDP flows from IoT devices causing NAT table churn and high memory pressure on the AP forwarding plane.
Zero Trust agent behavior: TLS sessions remain valid but underlying TCP sockets experience asymmetric packet drops leading to re-transmit and agent-level reconnect; no certificate issues found.
Reproduced in lab with mdns-replay at 3k qps causing AP CPU to hit 90% and zt-client to report socket resets within 2 minutes.
Temporary mitigation of blocking 224.0.0.0/4 on the affected access switch reduced symptom frequency immediately.
comments: Support (Aisha Malik) 2026-03-10: Initial triage: narrowed to 4th floor AP cluster after correlating helpdesk reports and AP telemetry. Escalated to Networking.

Networking (Carlos Rivera) 2026-03-10: Captured PCAP and conntrack dumps; hypothesis: uncontrolled multicast from IoT VLAN is flooding corporate-ssid due to bridging misconfiguration on one closet switch. Will apply temp ACL to drop mDNS on corporate SSID and monitor.

SRE (Lena Becker) 2026-03-10: Observed DNS latency spikes matching timestamps; recommend temporarily increasing core-dns worker threads and adding client-side DNS retry guidance to users while mitigation is applied.

Networking (Carlos Rivera) 2026-03-11: Temp ACL applied at 09:10 PDT dropping 224.0.0.0/4 on vlan-corp-ssid on closet-switch-4F; observed AP CPU fall from 96% to 35% and immediate reduction in zero-trust disconnects. Monitoring continues.
Support (Aisha Malik) 2026-03-12: Users report return-to-normal for 4th floor after mitigation; preparing follow-up runbook and firmware upgrade plan.
resolution_notes: Short-term (applied 2026-03-11): ACL to drop mDNS/LLMNR on corporate SSID on closet-switch-4F; moved a small set of known IoT devices to a new isolated SSID (iot-guest) on VLAN 220.
Medium-term (scheduled): Enable IGMP snooping and multicast rate limiting on all 4th floor leaf switches and WLC; scheduled for 2026-03-18 maintenance window.
Long-term (tracking): Aruba firmware vendor engaged; vendor triage indicates improved multicast handling in upcoming patch 6.4.x. Tracking PR to upgrade AP firmware once patch validated by WLAN team.
Config changes: increased conntrack max on APs from 16k to 32k as a safety valve (applied after-hours), and added monitoring alert for AP conntrack utilization >75%.
Runbook docs created: Confluence link and playbook for multicast storms and Zero Trust overlay impact. Follow-up task created to audit SSID bridging topology across all offices.
